body.text: Knowing how urgent care works in Istanbul before you arrive removes guesswork if a fever, sudden swelling, or unrelated illness develops after clinic hours. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders prepare clear local emergency contact sheets for every client without taking commissions from any hospital or clinic. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.
How does Türkiye's 112 emergency line work for English speakers?

Türkiye consolidated ambulance, police, fire, and disaster dispatch under the single [112 Emergency Call Centre](https://www.icisleri.gov.tr/tum-acil-numaralar-112de-toplandi), managed nationwide by the [Ministry of Interior's 112 Directorate](https://www.112.gov.tr/hakkimizda). Calls are free from any mobile or hotel phone, and operators can route English-speaking callers to foreign-language dispatchers, though handing the phone to a hotel receptionist is often fastest.

When calling 112 in a true emergency—such as chest pain, breathing difficulty, heavy bleeding, or loss of consciousness—state your exact location first: district, street name, hotel name, and room number. Say "English, ambulance" clearly and stay on the line. Because hotel front-desk staff in Istanbul are trained to relay exact Turkish addresses and cross-streets, alerting reception simultaneously can shave valuable minutes off ambulance arrival. Consular emergency lines, such as the [U.S. Consulate General Istanbul emergency page](https://tr.usembassy.gov/istanbul-emergency-contact/), should also be saved for citizen assistance if hospitalization occurs.
Which private hospitals in central Istanbul have 24/7 international ER desks?

Central Istanbul has several multi-specialty private hospitals operating 24/7 emergency departments that routinely admit foreign visitors, including facilities in Nişantaşı/Şişli, Topkapı, Levent, and Ataşehir. Note that Itinerary of Türkiye has zero commercial partnership or referral arrangement with any hospital; the examples below are listed strictly for geographic orientation.

During daytime hours, international patient offices handle registration and language coordination, while overnight admissions route directly through the Emergency Medicine desk. For example, [American Hospital (Amerikan Hastanesi)](https://www.amerikanhastanesi.org/patient-admission-process) in Teşvikiye/Nişantaşı refers after-hours arrivals directly to its 24/7 Emergency Medicine Desk and maintains an [International Visitors program](https://www.amerikanhastanesi.org/plan-your-visit/international-visitors). On the European side near Topkapı, [Koç University Hospital](https://www.kuh.ku.edu.tr/emergency-department) runs a 24/7 Emergency Service staffed by emergency medicine specialists alongside dedicated [International Visitors services](https://www.kuh.ku.edu.tr/plan-your-visit/international-visitors). Always confirm with your operating surgeon at discharge which specific ER they want you to visit if a post-op concern arises overnight.

body.text: What documents (passport, insurance policy, discharge summary) speed up ER intake?

Turkish hospital emergency departments accept foreign nationals without a referral, but intake moves faster when you hand over four items immediately: your original passport, your travel or medical insurance policy details, your signed surgical discharge summary, and a current list of medications and allergies.

Emergency physicians who did not perform your procedure need exact clinical facts within minutes. Your discharge summary tells them what surgery took place, which anesthesia and implants were used, and which anticoagulants or antibiotics you are currently taking. Keep a printed copy in your hotel room and a digital copy offline on your phone:

items: Original passport: Required by Turkish law for formal hospital registration.
Discharge summary (epikriz): Lists procedure date, surgical site, and operating physician's contact number.
Medication & allergy card: Includes exact dosages and any drug reactions.
Insurance policy & 24/7 assistance number: Clarify before travel whether your policy covers complications of elective procedures.
Payment card with international clearance: Private ERs often require a deposit before billing insurance.

faq.q: Is emergency hospital care free for tourists in Istanbul?
faq.a: No. While 112 emergency dispatch is free and hospitals stabilize urgent cases regardless of nationality, foreign visitors are billed for ER exams, imaging, and treatment unless covered by an accepted insurance policy.

faq.q: What is a nöbetçi eczane in Istanbul?
faq.a: A nöbetçi eczane is a rotating 24-hour duty pharmacy open overnight, on Sundays, and on public holidays. Every neighborhood posts the nearest duty pharmacy on closed pharmacy doors and municipal apps.

faq.q: Should I call my clinic or 112 first for chest pain or shortness of breath?
faq.a: Call 112 immediately for life-threatening symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or uncontrolled bleeding. Notify your clinic after emergency medical responders are engaged.

faq.q: Do private ER doctors in Istanbul speak English?
faq.a: Many emergency physicians at major central Istanbul private hospitals speak English, and international desks support translation during business hours, though overnight English coverage varies by shift.

faq.q: Will standard travel insurance cover post-op ER visits?
faq.a: Many standard travel policies exclude elective medical procedures and related complications. Check your policy wording before flying and consider specialized medical-travel coverage if needed.

faq.q: Can an ambulance take me to a specific private hospital?
faq.a: Public 112 ambulances transport patients to the nearest clinically appropriate hospital based on emergency triage rules; private hospital ambulances can be dispatched directly for non-critical transfers.
